correctness.rationale: Connected-tree bipartition is uniquely oriented by its unequal shore sizes m>4. The degree-excess identity sum_B(deg-1)=3 restricts nonleaf B vertices to k=1,2,3 and gives exactly four possible unlabeled cores. Each core carries four freely chosen pendant-leaf multiplicities and an explicitly identified automorphism action (S4,C2,S3,C2); nonisomorphic orbits match precisely the tree isomorphism types. Burnside yields all four generating summands and the exact coefficient identity for every m>=5. Full bipartite Prüfer enumeration independently identifies all 32,000 and 221,184 labeled spanning trees at m=5,6 and exactly 28/45 abstract types, with structural core lists matching; formal series coefficients tested to 40. Universal claim rests on proof, not finite computation.

originality.rationale: The complete Johnson–Nochumson 2026 source supplies broad partition bounds; Yan–Zhang 2026 supplies generic core asymptotics and already establishes the leading 29/144 coefficient, which is credited. Their published core proof discards symmetric leaf-vector collisions as lower-order error instead of enumerating the orbit corrections. The new classification of all four hub-core isomorphism types and complete exact Burnside series are not implied as stated by those bounds or asymptotic formulas; searches for alternate bicoloured-tree formulations, tables, and published-record searches found no covering theorem. Residual risk includes unsurfaced general Pólya formula or exact sequence database.
residual_risks: General unlabelled bicoloured-tree generating functions could contain an implicit coefficient formula not identified in the targeted source inspections.
Pippenger (2001) was abstract-only; its equal-class premise excludes the main m>4 target, but no full-content comparison was made.
Searches of published results and semantic records do not demonstrate absolute uniqueness; unindexed or unpublished work is not excluded.

value.rationale: The recently studied extremal benchmark K_(d,n-d) motivates obtaining exact (rather than merely asymptotic or bounded) type counts. Four hubs are the first small parameter with four different core symmetry groups and non-generic Burnside corrections. The theorem classifies every isomorphism type and provides one closed rational function for all m>=5, exact counts and quasipolynomial behaviour. This is a structural infinite-family enumeration, not a finite table or a substitution of the known cubic leading term; it isolates symmetry corrections essential for extending exact calculations to higher hub counts.
